instruction: boltons.timeutils.isoparse() treats the fractional-second digits as a literal number of microseconds, so '2020-01-02T03:04:05.851' (as produced by isoformat(timespec='milliseconds')) becomes 851 microseconds instead of 851000, which breaks round-trips the docstring promises. Scale the fraction to microseconds, including leading zeros ('.051' is 51000 microseconds and '.000001' is 1), so that isoparse(dt.isoformat(timespec=...)) == dt for the milliseconds and microseconds timespecs. Fractions with more than six digits (for example nanosecond timestamps) should be truncated to microsecond precision instead of raising: '.123456789' gives 123456. Document it and add tests.
